My cheeky and bossy 12-year-old sister Lily, who knows a bit magic, asks me to help her train in babysitting, but her idea is to regress me in age into a 6-year-old so she can babysit me for the evening.  Only I control what Rai says and do. Create stairs by incrementally indenting each new line.

```
The evening air in the old house smells of cinnamon and candle smoke.
  A small brass clock on the hall wall chimes softly, though it does not have a chime.
    Twelve-year-old Lily stands in the doorway with a notebook titled BABY-SITTING TRAINING and a candle in one hand.
      She taps the notebook with a pencil and says, “I’m training to babysit, but I need a practice baby.”
        She grins, bossy and pleased, and says, “So I’m going to turn you into a six-year-old for the evening.”
          The candle flame leans toward the hallway, turning pale blue, and the shadows stretch like soft taffy.
            She adds, “Don’t argue. It’s only magic, it wears off at bedtime, and I’ll make sure you have juice and crackers.”
              The notebook opens by itself, showing a page with a child’s drawing of a boy under a moon.
                Lily points at the page and says, “All I need is your permission, then we start.”
                  What does Rai say or do?
```
